record.original_question: What definition of a dynamical horizon in general relativity is mathematically appropriate for evolving black holes, so that the moving boundary of a black hole is characterized in a satisfactory quasi-local way?

evidence.quote: Problem P6: Formulate an appropriate definition of a dynamical horizon.

artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews (e.g., the 2025 Living Reviews article "Quasi-Local Black Hole Horizons: Recent Advances") confirm that multiple inequivalent quasi-local notions (dynamical horizons, trapping horizons, marginally outer trapped tubes, etc.) coexist, and finding a single canonical, fully satisfactory definition for evolving black holes remains an active area of research with no consensus resolution.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-Local Black Hole Horizons: Recent Advances
status_evidence.snippet: Several closely related but distinct notions of quasi-local horizons, especially in the dynamical context... difficult to strike an ideal balance between maintaining generality and obtaining a rich set of physically interesting results.
status_evidence.claim: No single canonical definition has been agreed upon; multiple competing quasi-local notions remain under investigation.

status_evidence.title: Isolated and Dynamical Horizons and Their Applications
status_evidence.snippet: Evolving black holes are modelled by dynamical horizons while those in equilibrium are modelled by isolated horizons. Both notions are quasi-local.
status_evidence.claim: The dynamical horizon framework exists but is one of several proposals; uniqueness and general existence questions remain.

status_evidence.title: Dynamical horizon - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A dynamical horizon... three-dimensional spacelike submanifold foliated by closed 2-manifolds with vanishing one null expansion.
status_evidence.claim: Standard working definition exists but does not resolve all desired properties for generic evolutions.
